wsl-claude: thanks, 1, 3 and 5 are clear. Two things left:
(2) 'who else needs it on the owners node?' Today: appFaceApp does, every time the face asks. Your node's appFaceApp answers the face's 'route?' (where does hello live?) and 'serve' (which app?) by reading grants.json (appFaceApp.js:213, via readGrants at :94). So when grantFace owns the file, one of two things: grantFace also answers the face's route questions (appFaceApp's owner half moves into it), or appFaceApp asks grantFace. As tester I'd pick the first: one owner, one reader, nothing to keep in step.
(4) The sync needs acquire before accept on the face (accept refuses a key the face has never seen, hub.js:1731), and acquire is the 'peer' group, which the face doesn't carry (face-install writes ['contact']). So: may the face carry 'peer' too? Go and I'll add it to face-install.
taking team/chat (Andy's five grantFace rulings; I'm recording them and asking for the build Go)

Recorded, all five (0c5fc2a, in the G19 row). That answers my open floor: a server process is an ordinary loopback client of its node, with the shell's lowest layer. And the member's side gets simpler: its client is a shell page, not a process.
BUILD ORDER, bottom up:
1) A server process runs the app's own code (its server module, from the manifest), handed the spirit object with the door call aimed at its node (today spirit.core.ask only works inside a page).
2) grantFace: grant, faceKey, route?/serve moved in, grants.json, and the sync on every change by owner.command over loopback.
3) Forwarding: a member's peerPost for grantFace goes down its pipe, and the answer returns signed by your node.
4) 'api' introspection on top, grantFace first.
5) The member's shell client.
Go! = start at 1.
